title: Lookups with a stale, too-long run-time hint, arriving in bursts
description: The same bursty key-value front end as w5: quick lookups, puts that sometimes flush, and ten-times-longer queries are all HIGH with one shared 100 us deadline, batch is NORMAL and bulk scans are LOW. The server's table of expected run times is out of date: it still says a lookup takes 20 us, as when lookups read from flash, although they now come from memory and take about 2 us. A scheduler that trusts this hint now runs lookups after the queries instead of before them, so during each burst a lookup waits through the whole backlog; only one that notices from observed run times that these '20 us' requests finish in a few microseconds can let them go first again.
changed_from_previous: w5 with the lookups' run-time hint wrong: the server says 20 us (longer than a query's 17 us) although a lookup takes about 2 us; the client's traffic, bursts, deadlines, classes, and all other hints are unchanged.
notes: Capacity, at 99.6 iterations per us (calibration.json); the client's traffic is identical to w5's, so the estimate is too: 13.60 us of fake work + 4.0 us overhead = 17.60 us per request, 8 / 17.60 us = 455k req/s; 300k/340k/365k/390k are 66/75/80/86% of it, and 390k was w5's measured headline. Bursts as in w4b and w5 (busy phase 624k req/s at 390k). Deadlines: 100 us for every HIGH kind, 5x the get's (wrong) 20 us hint and about 17x its real ~5.7 us. Ladder, against w5: inaccuracy 1 -> 2 (a kind's service_us is wrong, not only a hidden tail); no other dimension changes. The only edit is in the server's hint map, get service_us 2 -> 20: the cost table dates from when lookups read from flash. This error runs the opposite way from w5's: there a too-short hint pushed slow puts ahead of gets; here a too-long hint holds the scored kind back. Under sjf_guard a get's turn is arrival + 260 us, a query's arrival + 236 and a put's arrival + 108, so a get runs after every query that arrived before it or up to 24 us after it; its urgency guard thinks a get needs 20 us. sjf_rescue and sjf_learn rank a get as hint + 4 = 24 us against a query's 21 us, and sjf_learn's max(learned, hint) cannot correct a hint that is too long. Runqueue-wait check, from w5 at 390k: under sjf_guard gets wait 43.3 us at p99, under edf_high and prio, which rank gets with queries in arrival order, 120.3 and 119.7; so ranking gets with queries costs about 77 us of get runqueue wait at p99. Prediction: fifo, prio, edf_high, and fifo/ignore never read service_us, so they run exactly w5's experiment and should reproduce its numbers within noise (get p99 192 / 159 / 161.5 / 193 us at 390k); this is the built-in check. Under sjf_guard, get runqueue-wait p99 at 390k should rise from 43.3 to about 80-120 us and get p99 from 98.5 to about 130-165 us. A policy that learns from observed run times that '20 us' threads finish in about 6 us restores w5's order, worth about 85-100 us. Scans are LOW, so judge rule 4 still applies. No run.py changes are needed.
